source: English translation: Valmiki Ramayanam, IIT Kanpur (https://www.valmiki.iitk.ac.in/), via the MIT-licensed Valmiki Ramayan Dataset by Ashutosh Vijay.

verses.1: After Rama and the great-souled Bharata had spoken, Lakshmana then addressed Rama, the delight of the Raghus, with auspicious words.
verses.2: O delight of the Raghus, may the Ashwamedha, a great sacrifice and purifier of all sins, which is a purifier for you, the unconquerable one, be pleasing to you.
verses.3: Indeed, it is heard that in an ancient event, the very great-souled Indra, afflicted by the sin of Brahman-slaughter, was purified by the Ashwamedha sacrifice.
verses.4: O mighty-armed one, it is said that formerly, during the conflict between gods and asuras, there was a great Daitya named Vritra, renowned throughout the world.
verses.5: He was a hundred yojanas wide and three times that in height, and he regarded all three worlds everywhere with affection and love.
verses.6: He, being righteous, grateful, and perfected in intellect, ruled the vast and prosperous earth with perfect attention to dharma.
verses.7: While he was ruling, the earth became a wish-fulfilling cow, providing abundant and juicy roots and fruits.
verses.8: The earth, without cultivation, yielded abundant crops for that great-souled king, and he enjoyed such a prosperous and marvelous kingdom.
verses.9: A thought arose in his mind that he should perform unsurpassed penance, for indeed, penance is the supreme good, while other forms of happiness lead to delusion.
verses.10: He entrusted his eldest son, Madhureśvara, to the citizens and undertook severe penance, thereby causing all the deities to suffer.
verses.11: When Vritra was performing penance, Indra, greatly distressed, approached Vishnu and spoke these words.
verses.12: O mighty-armed one, Vritra, who is performing penance, has conquered the worlds; he is indeed powerful and righteous, and I am unable to control him.
verses.13: O Lord of Asuras, if he performs penance again, the worlds will remain subservient to him as long as they endure.
verses.14: And yet you disregard this extremely powerful Vritra; for indeed, Vritra would not exist even for a moment if you, O Lord of gods, were to become angry.
verses.15: Indeed, it was when he obtained your favor, O Vishnu, that he achieved lordship over the worlds from that time onwards.
verses.16: You, being well-composed, should bestow your favor upon the worlds, for by your action alone, the entire world would become peaceful and free from suffering.
verses.17: O Vishnu, all these gods indeed await you; therefore, render them great help by slaying Vritra.
verses.18: Indeed, you have always rendered help to these great-souled ones, for this task is unbearable for others, and you are the sole refuge for the helpless. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे चतुरशीतितमः सर्गः ।। 84 ।। Thus ends the eighty-fourth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
